title: The Last Harbor Revisited
premise: Hazel Eastwick, a ghostwriter who has spent her career erasing herself from other people's stories, takes an anonymous pen-pal assignment meant to pair strangers — but a clerical error pairs her with Julian Marsh, the rival memoirist whose book she is secretly writing and whose engagement she once broke by telling the truth. Their letters, unaware at first of each other's identities, force Hazel to confront the self-betrayal she sees in the mirror: she ghosted her own heart years ago when duty to her dying mother made her walk away from Julian without explanation. When the deception unravels and Julian learns she wrote both his memoir and their letters, Hazel must choose between the safe anonymity of her craft and claiming authorship of her own life; in the end, she publishes under her own name for the first time, and Julian meets her at the last harbor lighthouse where they first parted, choosing love over the pride that duty built between them.
about_author: Freya Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' letters before turning to fiction full-time. She writes romance about people who mistake silence for safety, and lives within sight of the sea.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Juggling two deadlines — Julian Marsh's rival memoir and a new anonymous pen-pal program run by her literary society — Hazel receives her assigned correspondent and feels an eerie familiarity in the handwriting she can't place. The emotional beat is restless unease: a woman who hides behind other voices senses one of them calling back.

chapters.title: Letters in Someone Else's Hand
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Hazel and Julian. Their correspondence deepens into startling honesty while, by day, they spar professionally over the memoir's direction, each unknowingly confiding in their enemy. The beat is dramatic irony tightening into intimacy — two people falling for the same soul wearing different names.

chapters.title: The Unmasking
chapters.summary: Julian's POV, then Hazel's. A leaked draft page reveals Hazel as his ghostwriter; cross-referencing phrasing, Julian realizes his tender correspondent and his ghost are the same woman who abandoned him years ago. He confronts her publicly at the memoir launch. The climax burns with betrayal on both sides — he was written by her, and never known.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returns
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Stripped of pseudonyms, Hazel publishes her own debut novel with a final chapter addressed to Julian, then waits at the harbor lighthouse where they once said goodbye. Julian arrives as the tide turns. The resolution lands on belonging: forgiveness begins with the woman in the mirror, and second chances belong to those brave enough to sign their own names.
